source_title: Michigan Board of State Canvassers certifies record-breaking 2026 General Election

corrections.evidence: Decision Desk HQ lists 2,615,251, 2,094,566 and 44,497 votes respectively and records its Benson call on November 3 at 10:45 p.m. EST. https://votes.decisiondeskhq.com/races/2026-11-03/michigan-governor-general-election

The timestamp of a count showing exactly 54.56% and 43.72%.
notes: NBC News, The Washington Post, Decision Desk HQ and MultiState all reported Benson’s win. Michigan’s official November candidate list confirms Anthony Hudson as the Libertarian gubernatorial candidate and omits Mike Duggan from that race. https://www.aol.com/articles/jocelyn-benson-wins-michigan-governor-061826000.html | https://www.washingtonpost.com/elections/results/2026/11/03/michigan-governor-benson-james-live-updates/ | https://www.multistate.us/elections/governor-race/michigan-2026 | https://elections.calhouncountymi.gov/November2026/docs/Official%20State%20Candidate%20List%20Nov.3.2026%20General.pdf

exact_quote: a utility may not energize a new or expanded electric service connection for a project
notes: Democratic Sen. Roland Gutierrez prefiled SB 296 on November 9 for the session opening January 12, 2027; it remained filed as of November 26. The two-year pause runs from enactment’s effective date and covers qualifying new projects and expansions. The bill requires local majority approval and an annual payment equal to the greater of 2% of attributable gross receipts or $10,000 per authorized megawatt. Payments are due March 1 and distributed equally to eligible host-county residents by June 1, less audited administrative expenses capped at 2%. https://capitol.texas.gov/reports/Report.aspx?ID=senatefiled&LegSess=90R | https://tlc.texas.gov/docs/legref/Dates-of-Interest.pdf

source_title: S. 3852 — Guaranteeing Rate Insulation from Data Centers Act
exact_quote: obtaining and maintaining an unexpired Zero Rate Effect Certificate

corrections.correct: During the ten-year transition, an existing covered center can continue using grid power only while it holds a valid certificate. Each certificate expires after one year.
corrections.evidence: Section 4 makes the certificate the condition for continued grid use during the transition. It does not give existing facilities an unconditional ten-year exemption.

corrections.correct: Planned sites would disclose estimates for their first operating year plus the next five years. Existing sites would disclose current-year and next-five-year estimates, plus actual use for up to five prior operating years.
corrections.evidence: Section 5(a) sets separate reporting periods for planned and existing facilities.

notes: Republican Josh Hawley introduced S. 3852 with Democrat Richard Blumenthal on February 11. The latest official action located was referral to Senate Energy and Natural Resources. The proposed power rule starts 180 days after enactment, covers facilities meeting the statutory 20-megawatt threshold and includes backup power. https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/BILLS-119s3852is

source_title: Thursday, November 19, 2026 — U.S. Senate Daily Press
exact_quote: By a vote of 62 to 33, the Senate passed H.R.2347, Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, as amended.

corrections.correct: Shelley Moore Capito (R) introduced S. 5653 on September 30, with Mike Lee (R), Sheldon Whitehouse (D) and Martin Heinrich (D). It was referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources.
corrections.evidence: The Government Publishing Office identifies the four senators, the September introduction date and the referral. https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/BILLS-119s5653is

corrections.field: bill number, votes and current status
corrections.correct: Both floor votes were on H.R. 2347. On November 9 the Senate voted 73–25 for cloture on the motion to proceed. On November 19 it passed the amended House bill 62–33 and sent it back to the House.
corrections.evidence: Roll call 257 names H.R. 2347. The November 19 Senate record identifies the amended measure carrying the permitting package. Senate floor debate was no longer pending on November 26. https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1192/vote_119_2_00257.htm | https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119hr2347eas/html/BILLS-119hr2347eas.htm

not_confirmed: Heinrich personally saying the bill codifies Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge. His support for making data centers pay their share is documented.
Trump personally using the codification wording; it appears in his administration’s official policy statement.
notes: The Senate-passed text bars recovery of covered incremental retail costs from other customers. The White House expressly said the bill would put Trump’s pledge into law, and the Center for Biological Diversity explicitly called the package a giveaway to the data-center industry. https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/SAP-S5653.pdf | https://biologicaldiversity.org/w/news/press-releases/senate-democrats-greenlight-environmental-catastrophe-by-advancing-permitting-reform-2026-11-18/
